page: Amazon Web Services c8gb.metal-48xl is a bare-metal compute-optimized instance built on the 64-bit ARM architecture using AWS Graviton processors. It features 192 dedicated physical cores and 192 vCPUs operating at 2.7 GHz with a single thread per core configuration, coupled with 384.0 GB of system memory. This hardware setup enforces a 2.0 GB memory-to-core ratio, tailored to computational throughput rather than massive memory footprint, while direct hardware access removes hypervisor overhead.

The platform does not include integrated local NVMe storage, meaning that all persistent and temporary file systems rely on network-attached storage options. Connectivity is supported by a 400 Gbps baseline network bandwidth interface. The architecture contains zero hardware graphics accelerators, and instruction execution is strictly ARM64-native, necessitating workloads that either run platform-agnostically or are compiled specifically for ARM instruction sets.

From an efficiency standpoint, the dedicated 192-core ARM topology provides high core density and predictable thread execution without resource contention from simultaneous multithreading. This hardware configuration is suitable for distributed high-performance computing, intensive batch processing, software compilation pipelines, large-scale video transcoding, and high-throughput containerized services.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gb.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, compute-optimized instance powered by 64-bit ARM AWS Graviton processors. The system delivers 192 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.7 GHz with a 1:1 core-to-thread layout, eliminating hypervisor overhead and simultaneous multithreading penalties. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of memory, maintaining a 2.0 GB per core allocation suited for compute-intensive demands. The instance features no local storage, requiring network-attached block devices, and does not include GPU acceleration. Networking is backed by a 400 Gbps baseline bandwidth pipe, facilitating massive bidirectional data throughput. The arm64 processor design provides high density and energy-efficient execution for native multithreaded binaries. This server is best suited for high-density container clustering, continuous integration pipelines, batch data crunching, distributed microservices, and network-bound scientific modeling requiring direct hardware access.
